notes: Perfect claim overlap (C71, C72, C73) regarding Pfs25 mRNA female-specificity. LLM finds authors appropriately acknowledged this limitation, while peer reviewers express concern that sex ratio changes may alter the relationship shape, indicating uncertainty about measurement validity.

High overlap on age effects (C64, C65). LLM finds age-dependent infectivity supported by data and prior evidence, while peer reviewers state confidence intervals suggest no clear effect, questioning the statistical evidence.

Shared claims about children's gametocyte burden and transmission contribution (C6, C42, C101, C123). LLM finds cross-sectional data adequate despite adult feeding assay limitation, while peer reviewers question temporal generalizability and request seasonal context.

Substantial overlap on non-linear relationship claims (C35, C46, C47, C48, C52). LLM finds the double-hump pattern robustly demonstrated with proper statistical methods, while peer reviewers find it 'unintuitive' with 'huge uncertainty range' and question whether model choice forced the pattern.

Good overlap on asexual parasite density inclusion (C58, C59, C60). Both express uncertainty about mechanistic interpretation. LLM notes unclear mechanism and potential confounders; peer reviewers question rationale and note it modifies parameter interpretation.

Moderate overlap on low-density transmission efficiency (C4, C5, C46, C47). LLM finds experimental support for efficient low-density infection, while peer reviewers question the non-linear pattern and note huge uncertainty ranges.

Shared claims on uncertainty handling methodology (C74-C78). LLM finds Bayesian approach appropriately handles measurement uncertainty, while peer reviewers request expanded discussion of uncertainties, parameter drivers, and model superiority justification.

Overlap on QT-NASBA methodology and uncertainty propagation (C66, C67, C68, C106, C114). LLM finds simultaneous fitting appropriately propagates uncertainty, while peer reviewers question method choice justification, female-only detection concerns, and request validation on independent data.
Both agree on the appropriateness of acknowledging the adult feeding assay limitation (C131). LLM and peer reviewers both recognize this as an important caveat affecting transmission estimates.

Minimal overlap (C8) on intervention efficacy predictions. Both express uncertainty: LLM notes predictions are untested inferences; peer reviewers raise major concerns about efficacy definition and translation to human infection reduction.

Small overlap on model selection (C115, C121). LLM finds DIC-based model selection appropriate, while peer reviewers request quantitative comparison of alternative models in main text and question model superiority evidence.

Minimal overlap (C55) on submicroscopic transmission estimates. Both express uncertainty: LLM notes extrapolation to low densities with high measurement error; peer reviewers question negative binomial choice and suggest zero-inflated models may be more appropriate.
Small overlap (C3, C113) on basic experimental design. Both accept the 171 feeding assay data collection methodology as sound, though peer reviewers raise concerns about interpretation and analysis.

Small overlap (C45, C100) on intervention implications. LLM finds logical inference from low-density transmission data, while peer reviewers question how gametocyte density reduction translates to mosquito infection and human incidence reduction.
Minimal overlap (C121, C122) on model comparison. LLM finds model selection properly justified, while peer reviewers want quantitative goodness-of-fit comparisons in main manuscript.
Minimal overlap (C138) on overdispersion characterization. LLM finds it well-characterized, while peer reviewers question whether negative binomial adequately fits data with many zeros.

LLM evaluates intervention efficacy predictions (C8, C36, C38-C40, C44, C102-C104) as uncertain due to lack of actual intervention data. No direct peer review match, though R10 addresses related efficacy definition concerns.

LLM expresses uncertainty about 30% submicroscopic transmission estimate (C55-C57, C127) due to extrapolation. Peer R9 partially addresses with statistical model concerns, but no complete match for this specific transmission percentage claim.

Peer reviewers question age-gametocyte density model (C124) stating model and parameters not explained, equation derivation unclear, and Figure 2A fit poor for two age groups. No direct LLM result addresses this specific modeling concern.

Peer reviewers question direct evidence for parasite strategies at low densities like sex ratio alteration (C49-C51), stating no direct information obtained. No corresponding LLM evaluation of these specific mechanistic speculation claims.

Peer reviewers support the observation about lack of uncertainty reporting in literature (C69), praising authors' uncertainty quantification approach. No direct LLM evaluation of this meta-observation about field practices.
